architecture: OpenLens Core System — VS Code & Snowflake Integration
description: Machine-verifiable architecture boundary rules for OpenLens. Load this file into the Dev scanner via the architecture_rules_path scan parameter.

adrs.title: Two-Mode Architecture: Dev in VS Code, Archy in Web Workspace
adrs.decision: Provide code-level maintainability in the VS Code extension and system-level visual design in the Archy web workspace, connected by shared rules and a common API.
adrs.consequences: Prevents IDE bloat while giving developers a dedicated visual workspace for complex diagrams and trade-off evaluations.

adrs.title: Deterministic Local AST Analysis with Fail-Safe Offline Mode
adrs.decision: Perform all core duplication and linter checks locally via Python AST without requiring cloud availability or Snowflake access.
adrs.consequences: Ensures immediate editor feedback (<50ms) and complete user privacy for proprietary codebases.

adrs.title: Snowflake for Knowledge and Evaluation — Not for Raw Source Code
adrs.decision: Use Snowflake only for curated architecture patterns, library metadata, anonymised benchmark cases, and aggregate analytics. No raw source code or secrets transmitted by default.
adrs.consequences: Enables enterprise-grade retrieval quality while preserving developer privacy and hackathon compliance.

adrs.title: Provider-Neutral Model Gateway with Local-First Routing
adrs.decision: All inference requests go through a provider-neutral ModelGatewayAdapter interface. Local adapters (Ollama) are preferred. Remote adapters require explicit user consent and ALLOW_REMOTE=true.
adrs.consequences: Users can run the full AI feature set locally on open-weight models without any cloud dependency.

rules.name: No Raw Source Code to External APIs
rules.description: OpenLens Dev must never transmit unredacted source code, file paths, or credentials to model gateways or Snowflake without explicit user consent and secret redaction.
rules.rationale: Protects proprietary code and user privacy as a primary product principle.

rules.name: Frontend Must Not Import Database Models Directly
rules.description: Frontend layer components (VS Code Webview, Archy web) must not directly import or query database models. All data access goes through the backend API.
rules.rationale: Enforces layer separation and prevents tight coupling between presentation and persistence.

rules.name: Archy Rules Must Be Versioned Before Export
rules.description: Architecture rules exported from Archy to Dev must include a version field and source_decision_id. Versionless rules are rejected by Dev.
rules.rationale: Ensures Dev can detect stale rules and trace every constraint to a recorded decision.

rules.name: Local Checks Must Run Without Snowflake
rules.description: Deterministic AST checks (duplication, unused imports, complexity) must complete successfully when Snowflake is unreachable. Snowflake is supplementary, never a hard dependency.
rules.rationale: Guarantees developer value and privacy-preserving offline operation.

rules.name: Model Output Must Not Execute Shell Commands
rules.description: Language model output must be treated as a proposal, not an instruction. No model output may directly execute shell commands, apply file edits, or install packages without explicit user approval.
rules.rationale: Prevents prompt injection and maintains developer control as a core product principle.

rules.name: Secret Redaction Before Remote Calls
rules.description: All payloads destined for external services (model gateways, Snowflake) must pass through the secret redaction filter before transmission.
rules.rationale: Never intentionally transmit detected secrets to language models or cloud services.
